definitions.explanation: The formal ritual of exchanging business cards when meeting someone in a professional setting. A key part of Japanese business etiquette.

examples.japanese: ⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しましょう→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{済|す}ませた→済む：01950_sumu⟧。
examples.english: We finished exchanging business cards before the meeting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In Japan, the etiquette of exchanging business cards is considered very important.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{名刺|めいし}→名刺：01090_meishi⟧ (business card) + ⟦{交換|こうかん}→交換：02746_koukan⟧ (exchange). In Japanese business culture, this ritual follows specific rules of etiquette.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to exchange business cards
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{済|す}ませる→済ませる：02121_sumaseru⟧: to finish exchanging cards
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧: business card exchange etiquette

CULTURAL NOTE:
When exchanging business cards in Japan, one should present the card with both hands, with the text facing the recipient. Received cards should be treated respectfully — never written on, bent, or placed carelessly. During a meeting, received cards are typically lined up on the table in front of you as a reference.
